First of all, people need income. As a business owner, you can afford to pay people a decent income if, and only if, they are productive enough so that work generates enough profit to cover all of the costs, plus their wages, plus the needed profits. This condition is non negotiable. It must be met.

The problem is the current workforce does not have the skill base, and they are not going to get it from school. They have to get it from you.

So, your business needs to be involved in something very profitable. Ignore everything else. You are going to need that money.

Then, your business needs to become half business, half school. You become not just an owner operator, but also a teacher. You'll have to bring these people in raw, and train them on the job. Wages go up only after productivity goes up. You are building a skilled employee base. As their skills increase, they earn you more money, and their wages increase as well.

Turns out, workers like this system... it rewards them for improved performance, and incentivizes further improved performance. They become part of the team/family, working together toward a better future. Humans just prefer it that way. You promote internally. If you need something new, you teach yourselves how to do it. You train your trainees today so they can become your managers tomorrow.

This is not unlike the apprenticeship approach employed by skilled laborers for thousands of years. It's a proven system.

Now, you can stone soup this thing if you need to get it started. People will work for free to learn how to become valuable, if they think it is going to lead to a job. I used to call it a volunteer workplace training program - or a work placement, if you will. Workers get job experience, some training, and a decent reference for their resume. Local welfare officials will often agree to allow a new worker to continue collecting welfare while working for you for free in exchange for training. I used to get six months coverage from welfare.

The upside for you is you get to evaluate a person for an extended period before formally hiring them. Hiring is a very risky activity.
